measured.description: The requested position itself, the same spot in every exposure: no motion was given, and no Gaia star (G < 17) is within 3 arcsec of it in 2026.

stars_in_circle.note: Gaia DR3 stars (G < 17) whose place falls inside the measuring circle (radius_arcsec) around the object, per visit (by_epoch, at the visit's middle date) and over the whole run (stars: nearest and farthest distance, visits). Their light is part of every flux measured there, and nothing is subtracted, so a flux with such a star in the circle is the sum of both. Sources Gaia does not list, or lists fainter than G = 17, are not included; in the infrared some of them are bright. Stars further out can still fall in the wider ring of the wing measure.

method.flux: Sum of the zodi-subtracted image in a circle of radius 2.5 native pixels (15.4 arcsec) on the object's expected position, minus the local sky (clipped median in a ring 14 to 20 pixels out), times the pixel solid angle. No aperture correction, so values are a few per cent below total flux.
method.error: 1 sigma: the archive's VARIANCE image and the uncertainty of the sky level (flux_err_stat_mjy), with 3 per cent of the flux added in quadrature (flux_err_mjy), the extra scatter the Explanatory Supplement reports for repeated measurements.
method.rejection: A measurement has a number only if no pixel in the circle carries a flag of the Explanatory Supplement's photometry list (SUR_ERROR, NONFUNC, MISSING_DATA, HOT, COLD, NONLINEAR, PERSIST, BLOOM, SNOWBALL, HALO, SATELLITE_HALO) or is empty. 'saturated' means a pixel overflowed within the first seconds (OVERFLOW with SUR_ERROR), received charge from a saturated neighbour (BLOOM) or could not be linearised (NONLINEAR). OVERFLOW alone is kept: the pixel reached half of full well and its value comes from the reads before that; overflow_pixels counts them.

statuses.flagged: a flagged pixel in the circle, no flux given
statuses.no_data: an empty pixel in the circle
statuses.no_sky: too few clean pixels for the sky level
statuses.off_image: too close to the edge of the detector

method.wing: wing_mjy is a relative brightness from unsaturated pixels, NOT a flux. It is the same sky-subtracted sum in a ring around the star (wing_ring_px, in native pixels, chosen once per detector), where only a few per cent of the star's light falls, plus any fainter star in the ring. Compare it only with other wing values of the same star in the same wavelength bin. A ring is used if it holds no saturated pixel and at most a tenth of it is flagged; flagged pixels are left out (wing_clean_fraction). Use it only where wing_trusted is true (detectors 5 and 6): there, two values of an unchanged star in one bin agree to about 5 per cent (worst seen 16 per cent in detector 5, 68 in detector 6). In detectors 1 to 4 they can disagree by a factor of two, so those values say nothing reliable about variability.
